en.name: Pollock
en.summary: Pollock is a lean, mild white fish and the workhorse behind fish fingers and surimi. From purchase the fresh fillets keep 1–2 days in the fridge and 4–8 months in the freezer.
en.pantry: Fresh pollock does not keep at room temperature. It is a lean fish with soft flakes that go slack quickly once warm, and much of what is sold at a counter was frozen at sea and thawed for display, which means its clock started long before you saw it. Bring it home cold and follow the 2-hour rule, or 1 hour above 32 °C (90 °F). If the fillet was sold as previously frozen, do not refreeze it raw.
en.fridge: Keep pollock at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, on a rack over ice in a container that catches the melt water, and cook it within 1–2 days from purchase. Do not let it sit in liquid; pollock takes up water and goes mushy faster than a firmer white fish. Store it in a single layer on the bottom shelf, below anything ready to eat. Ask the counter whether it was previously frozen — with pollock it very often was, and the answer changes what you can do with it.
en.freezer: Pollock keeps 4–8 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Lean flesh freezes well, but pollock fillets are soft and thin and burn easily, so wrap tightly with no air pockets or ice-glaze them first by dipping in cold water. Freeze in meal-sized portions, flat, and label the date. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the months are about quality. Commercially frozen-at-sea pollock is usually better than anything you can freeze at home, so buying it frozen is no compromise.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge overnight on a plate, or in a sealed bag under cold running water. Never on the counter or in warm water. Pat it dry, cook it promptly, and do not refreeze raw fish.
spoilage: A sour or ammoniacal smell instead of a clean, mild one.
Flesh that stays dented when pressed rather than springing back.
Flakes that gape apart, or a milky film on the fillet.
A grey or yellow cast where the flesh should be white.
tips: Ask whether it was previously frozen; if so, cook it rather than refreezing.
Keep it on a rack over ice, never in melt water.
Ice-glaze before freezing — thin soft fillets burn quickly.
Buy frozen-at-sea pollock without hesitation; it is often the better fish.

faq.q: How long does pollock keep in the fridge?
faq.a: 1–2 days from purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, on ice and not sitting in water.
Yes, 4–8 months at −18 °C, wrapped airtight or ice-glazed. Do not refreeze a fillet that was sold thawed.

faq.q: Is pollock the fish in fish fingers and surimi?
faq.a: Usually, yes. Alaska pollock is the main species used for both, which is why it is one of the most-caught fish in the world.

faq.q: How can you tell if pollock has gone off?
faq.a: A sour or ammoniacal smell, a milky film, gaping flakes, or flesh that will not spring back when pressed.

zh.name: 狹鱈
zh.summary: 狹鱈是味道溫和的低脂白肉魚，也是魚柳條和魚漿（蟹味棒）背後的主力魚種。生鮮魚片從購買日起冷藏可放 1～2 天，冷凍 4～8 個月。
zh.pantry: 新鮮狹鱈不耐室溫。它是低脂魚，肉片鬆軟，一回溫就迅速鬆散；而且櫃上賣的很多其實是船凍後解凍陳列的，也就是說它的時鐘在你看到之前早就開始走了。請保冷帶回家，守 2 小時原則，室溫超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時。若標示是解凍品，生的就不要再冷凍。
zh.fridge: 架在網架上、下面鋪冰，容器要能接住融水，放 4 °C 以下，並在購買後 1～2 天內煮掉。不要讓它泡在液體裡；狹鱈吸水後變糊的速度比質地緊實的白肉魚快得多。單層平放在最下層，位置低於所有即食食品。買的時候問一下是不是解凍品——狹鱈很常是，而答案會改變你接下來能怎麼處理它。
zh.freezer: 狹鱈在 −18 °C 下可放 4～8 個月。低脂魚肉耐凍，但狹鱈魚片又軟又薄、很容易凍燒，所以要包緊不留空氣，或先浸冷水做冰鍍。按一餐的量壓平分裝並標日期。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，月數講的是品質。船上急速冷凍的狹鱈通常比你在家能凍出來的好，所以買冷凍品一點都不吃虧。
zh.thawing: 放盤子上冷藏隔夜解凍，或密封裝袋用冷水沖。不要放室溫或泡溫水。擦乾後盡快烹調，生魚不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸或有氨味，而不是乾淨溫和的魚味。
按壓後凹陷回不來，而不是有彈性。
肌肉纖維裂開，或魚片表面出現乳白薄膜。
本該白皙的魚肉泛灰或泛黃。
tips: 問清楚是不是解凍品；是的話就煮掉，不要再冷凍。
架在網架上放冰的上方，不要泡融水。
冷凍前做冰鍍——又薄又軟的魚片很快凍燒。
放心買船凍狹鱈，品質常常更好。

faq.a: 鋪冰、不泡水，放 4 °C 以下，從購買日起 1～2 天。
可以，−18 °C 下 4～8 個月，密封包好或做冰鍍。解凍品不要再冷凍。

faq.q: 魚柳條和蟹味棒用的是狹鱈嗎？
faq.a: 通常是。阿拉斯加狹鱈是這兩者的主要原料，也因此成為全球捕獲量最大的魚種之一。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷狹鱈不新鮮了？
faq.a: 發酸或氨味、表面乳白薄膜、肌肉纖維裂開，或按壓沒有彈性。
